subject: Planned orchestration safeguard: WestUS4 rolling driver updates & preflight
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme-retail.com>, CloudPartner Ops <ops@cloudpartner.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Planned orchestration safeguard: WestUS4 rolling driver updates & preflight

Hi Elena / team,

We have a scheduled maintenance window for the WestUS4 region on 2026-08-10 from 01:00–05:00 UTC. This is a staged driver/kernel refresh targeted at a small set of NIC firmware variants that we’ve identified as having elevated hang risk under long-lived connections.

What to expect:
- Rolling node restarts across host pools with 30–45s graceful drain per pod.
- Automatic retrying and request replay where safe; brief 5–10 minute elevated error rates are a conservative expectation during the warm-up of routes.
- We will run a customer canary for your dedicated tenancy (if you opt in) in the earlier slot on 2026-08-09 to validate traffic handling.

Attachments: preflight-checklist.pdf (PDF, 120KB) — contains the preflight steps, KV cache hints, and recommended client retry settings.

Action requested: please confirm by EOD 2026-08-04 whether Acme would like the dedicated canary and if there are blackout constraints we should avoid. If no reply, we’ll presume standard scheduling and run the canary for a short 30-minute validation window.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-08-westus4

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme-retail.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Security Team <sec@acme-retail.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 09:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned orchestration safeguard: WestUS4 rolling driver updates & preflight

Thanks, Avery. Quick questions:
1) For the short elevated error period you mention, can you estimate percent of affected requests and whether that counts against our SLA?
2) We'd like the canary but request that it target only the read-only subset of our traffic and run no later than 2026-08-09 23:00 UTC.
3) Do you have any logs or trace snapshots from the firmware variant you're targeting? Our security lead copied here will want to review.

On initial read it looks low risk but we need to be explicit about retries — we prefer idempotent retries at the client level.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director of Platform Engineering, Acme Retail
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 10:10:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned orchestration safeguard: WestUS4 rolling driver updates & preflight

Hi all,

Short answers and plan details:
- Expected impact: we estimate ~1–3% of requests may transiently return 5xx during warm-up; historically any customer-visible spike has been under 10 minutes for a full region rollout when canaries succeed. SLA credit: we'll handle exceptions on a case-by-case basis — please flag any business-impacting errors and we'll escalate immediately.

- Canary: we can run a read-only canary for Acme on 2026-08-09 22:00–22:30 UTC (fits Elena's constraint). We will use traffic shaping to restrict to read-only endpoints only.

- Logs: attaching the internal rollback plan and a short trace extract from a prior firmware rollout that shows the hang signature (rollback-plan.md). We cannot share raw host-level logs publicly but can provide sanitized traces and the observability slices your security team needs.

Mitigation strategy: staged driver swap + rolling restart -> warmup -> 15m observation -> proceed. If we detect >5% sustained errors or persistent connection hangs, we stop and roll back to the prior driver and route traffic to the fallback model pool.

I’ll schedule a 30 min preflight call if Acme confirms the canary.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
[attachment: rollback-plan.md (text, 8KB)]
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned orchestration safeguard: WestUS4 rolling driver updates & preflight

Elena — thanks for the quick turn. Confirming the canary slot for Acme: 2026-08-09 22:00–22:30 UTC (read-only). Monica will run the canary and provide real-time telemetry through the status page. We will also share a sanitized trace bundle after the canary and again after the full rollout.

I created a short calendar invite (canary-schedule.ics) for the 22:00 slot — please accept if that works. If we see any regressions during the canary we will not proceed with the full region rollout and will notify you within 15 minutes of detection.

Post-maintenance: we’ll send a 24–48 hour postmortem and a draft of action items; if there is customer impact we will follow the standard SLA review and remediation steps.

Thanks,
Avery
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena@acme-retail.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 05:30:12 -0700
Subject: Post-maintenance summary: WestUS4 rolling update completed (brief)

Team — short summary of what we observed during the 01:00–05:00 UTC window:
- Status: full region rollout completed at 04:42 UTC. Canary for Acme at 22:00 UTC the previous day completed with no client-facing errors.
- Incident: between 02:17–02:24 UTC we observed an elevated 5xx rate affecting ~2% of total requests (7-minute window). Root cause: transient NIC driver hang on a specific firmware revision that caused TCP stalls for a subset of hosts.
- Mitigation: automatic retry logic plus a controller-triggered evacuation of the three affected hosts reduced the error window; we applied a targeted rollback on those hosts and re-deployed the prior driver image. No customer data loss.

Action items (short):
1) Immediate: provide sanitized traces and a timeline to Acme (attached: postmortem-draft.md).
2) 48h: full postmortem and mitigation plan (firmware-compatibility gating + expanded canaries).
3) 14-day: expanded regression test adding longer-lived connection profiles.

We will follow up with the full postmortem document and a proposed schedule for the regression test.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Site Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: postmortem-draft.md (text, 14KB)]
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@acme-retail.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-maintenance summary: WestUS4 rolling update completed (brief)

Thanks for the update — the short window aligns with what we saw on our side (a small spike of 502s for background inventory sync). Two asks:
1) Can you provide the sanitized traces you mentioned and a short list of hosts affected (IDs are fine, no raw logs)?
2) We’d like the account team to open the SLA review process; please advise expected next steps for credit calculation.

If you can send the sanitized traces and the draft postmortem by EOD Friday (2026-08-13) we can triage internally and decide on credit requests.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director of Platform Engineering, Acme Retail
